{"bytes":355630,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","durationMs":6840,"result":"# Testing Subgrid Support: Positive vs. Negated @supports Queries\n\nBased on the MDN documentation provided, **testing the positive form is the recommended approach** for feature detection, though both methods work.\n\n## Recommended Approach (Positive Form)\n\n```css\n@supports (grid-template-rows: subgrid) {\n  /* Apply subgrid-dependent styles */\n  .grid-container {\n    grid-template-rows: subgrid;\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Why Positive Testing is Preferred\n\n1. **Clarity and Intent**: The positive form directly expresses what you're checking for\n2. **Fallback Design**: Modern CSS follows a progressive enhancement pattern where non-supporting browsers ignore unsupported rules anyway\n3. **Standard Practice**: The documentation emphasizes this pattern throughout\n\n## The Negated Form (Works, But Less Ideal)\n\n```css\n@supports not (grid-template-rows: subgrid) {\n  /* Fallback for browsers without subgrid support */\n  .grid-container {\n    display: grid;\n    grid-template-rows: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Known Pitfalls with Negated Queries\n\nWhile the negated form is syntactically valid per the specification, there are practical concerns:\n\n1. **Double Maintenance**: You maintain both positive and negative rule sets, increasing complexity\n2. **Readability**: Negated conditions are harder to read and understand at a glance\n3. **Browser Fallback Already Exists**: Browsers that don't support `grid-template-rows: subgrid` will simply ignore that declaration anyway, making explicit negation redundant\n\n## Best Practice\n\nUse the **positive form with optional fallbacks**:\n\n```css\n/* Default/fallback styles */\n.grid-container {\n  display: grid;\n  grid-template-rows: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr));\n}\n\n/* Enhanced styles for supporting browsers */\n@supports (grid-template-rows: subgrid) {\n  .grid-container {\n    grid-template-rows: subgrid;\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThis approach is more maintainable and aligns with the progressive enhancement philosophy discussed in the CSS documentation.","url":"https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@supports"}
